text: Fuga Daemonum (Japanese: , Goumashouhazan) is Corvin's Level I Blade Special in .
Frost Queen is Dahlia's Level III Blade Special in . Frost Queen is also Dahlia's Special Art during Merc Assault missions in the .
Frost Banish (Japanese: , Furosutigubanisshu, Lit. "Frostig Banish") is Theory's Level II Blade Special in .
Fruit Spouters are weapons in Xenoblade Chronicles: Future Connected. They are gunberries wielded by Kino.
Fruit Bouncers are weapons in Xenoblade Chronicles: Future Connected. They are gunberries wielded by Kino.
Fruit Lobbers are weapons in Xenoblade Chronicles: Future Connected. They are gunberries wielded by Kino.
The Gamma, Main Approach (Japanese: , Koronī Ganma: Seidōguchi) is a Landmark in , located on Melnath's Shoulder. It serves as the main entrance into Colony Gamma.
Ghondor Vandham (Japanese: ゴンドウ・ヴァンダム, Gondō Vandamu), or simply named Ghondor, is a character in . She was designed by Masatsugu Saito, the lead character designer of the game.

Gallivanter Buckley (Japanese: , Jibashiri no Bakkuru) is a Unique Monster in . It is a member of the Hox family, and can be found at level 30 near the Titan Rock at Great Cotte Falls. The Sandsmoke Skill can be earned for the Soulhacker class by defeating it.
The Gamma Canteen (Japanese: , Koronī Ganma: Yagai Shokudō) is a Rest Spot in . It is located in Colony Gamma on Melnath's Shoulder. The Meat 'n' Veg Leclati can be purchased here.

The Garf Mine Track (Japanese: , Fureveru Hanshutsudō, Frevel Export Road) is a Landmark in . It is located in the Urayan Tunnels of the Pentelas Region, and connects to the Tunnels Entrance in the Fornis Region.
The Generator Control Room (Japanese: , Hatsudensho Shikishitsu) is a Rest Spot in . It is located in the Urayan Tunnels.
|-|Common = |-|Rare = |-|Legendary = Fur Socks are Accessories in and . The legendary variant can be obtained from Indiscreet Gombaba.

|-|Common = |-|Rare = |-|Legendary = Gear Supports are Accessories in and . The common variant can be purchased from the Colony 4 Commissary. The legendary variant can be purchased at the Prize X-change Red or obtained from Scornful Daria. In , the common variant can be purchased from the Elevator Landing Caravan.
The Gamma, Assembly Yard (Japanese: , Koronī Ganma Shūkaijō) is a Landmark in . It is located in Colony Gamma on Melnath's Shoulder.
The Gamma, Back Way (Japanese: , Koronī Ganma: Uramichiguchi) is a Landmark in . It is located in Colony Gamma on Melnath's Shoulder.
Galghour's Menhir (Japanese: , Gūga no Kyogan) is a Landmark in . It is located next to Piento Basin in the Eagus Wilderness.
The Fuller Elevator Landing (Japanese: , Furā Erebētā-mae) is a Landmark in . It is located in the Great Sword's Base. The elevator leading to the hilt of Swordmarch is located here.

Fuschian Fields (Japanese: , Kōshi Senkyō) is a Secret Area in , located in Millick Meadows. It becomes accessible from Murmur Rise after the party enters Origin for the first time. This is the only location where the Vvarga enemy family can be found, including the Unique Monster Wicked Wolf Aranqui.
Gava Junction (Japanese: , Gava no Sansaro) is a Landmark in . It is located on Captocorn Peak.
The Gardin Defense Base (Japanese: , Gādin Bōei Kichi) is a Location in . It is located on the Syra Hovering Reefs. After The Castle Guard, numerous Keves Forces appear here.

Galloping Ghuldan (Japanese: , Shunkyaku no Gorutān) is a Unique Monster in . It is a member of the Ellook family, and can be found at level 56 near the Lost Colony in Farlaine Underpass in Erythia Sea. The Apothecary's Wisdom Skill can be earned for the Soulhacker class by defeating it.
Funicular Approach (Japanese: , Daishakō Erebētā-mae ) is a Landmark in . It is located at the Agnus Castle Barbican in the Cadensia Region.
Gerran Amoneys (Japanese: , Geran Amonē) are Minor Enemies in . They are members of the Amoney family, and can be found at level 58-59 in Coolley Lake on Melnath's Shoulder.
Gemini Controllers are Collectible items in . They can be found in the Origin. They can also be produced from the Atoll Ferronis Hulk Fabricator after Origin has been reached for the first time.
Gastrates Ether Furnaces are items in . It drops from Gastrates type Levnises.
Gastrates Gun Turrets are items in and . They can drop from Gastrates-type Levnises. In , they can be dropped by Stronghammer Dorga.
Full-Bodied Ardun Meats are items in . They can be obtained from the Ardun family of enemies. The rare variant can also be purchased from Sunny & Cheerio's Caravan.
Garaffa Tenderloins are items in . They can be obtained from the Garaffa enemy family. The rare variant can also be purchased from Sunny & Cheerio's Caravan.

Full-Filling Crispygrills are Meal items in . They can be cooked by Manana at Rest Spots. One Silver Nopon Coin can be used to cook this meal instead of the necessary ingredients. It can be unlocked by purchasing the Riverbird Crispygrill from the Colony Iota Canteen for the first time.
General Antols are Normal Minor Enemies in . They are members of the Antol family, and can be found at level 61-62 in Malevolent Hollow in Erythia Sea.
The Gamma Commissary is a shop in . It is run by a Colony Gamma Soldier and can be found in Colony Gamma on Melnath's Shoulder.

Gastrates (Japanese: , Gatoratesu) are minor enemies in . They are Kevesi Levnises, and can be found at level 38-39 near the south entrance to Keves Castle in the Syra Hovering Reefs, near Protector Revelta. They can also be found at level 66-67 on the south-eastern side of Lavi Sandbar in Erythia Sea. Valdi's Levnis project Dorrick is a type of Gastrates Levnis.
The Gamma, Staging Yard is a Location in . It is located in Colony Gamma on Melnath's Shoulder.

|-|Common = |-|Rare = |-|Legendary = Ghillie Masks are Accessories in and . The common variant can be purchased from the O'Virbus Commissary and Handypon. In , the legendary variant can be obtained from Troglodyte Umir.

|-|Common = |-|Rare = |-|Legendary = Gale Leg Frames are Accessories in and . The common variant can be purchased from the Illicit Caravan. The legendary variant can be acquired by defeating Puzzled Raquinu. In , the legendary variant can be obtained from Perambulator Moritz.
Gambert is a NPC in who can be found in Colony Iota and Colony 30.
Full Weak Guards are DLC Accessories in . They can be purchased from Prize X-change Red in the Land of Challenge for 6000 Noponstones.
Fury Reaper is a Battle Art in . It is a variant of Havoc Slayer that can only be used by Segiri.

Furious Flash (Japanese: , Ressen) is a Battle Art in . It is a variant of Spearpoint Thrust that can only be used by Teach. He swings his staff in circles before striking an enemy with a swing to the right.
Geo Breaker is a Battle Art in . It is one of Monica's arts as a Hero, which is a variant of Mighty Beat used by Ouroboros.

Gatling Peck is a Battle Art in . It is an art of the Soulhacker class. It is acquired by defeating the Unique Monster Heavenrazor Egreet while the Soul Hack skill is set on any player-controlled party member.

Gauntlet: Beginner is an Archsage's Gauntlet Challenge in . It can be received from Nopon Archsage in the Land of Challenge, available as downloadable content from the third part of the Expansion Pass. Clearing this challenge with at least a B rank for the first time will unlock the Throwback A outfit for Sena and clearing with at least A rank for the first will unlock the Throwback A outfit for Lanz.

Gauntlet: Intermediate is an Archsage's Gauntlet Challenge Battle in . It can be challenged by talking to the Nopon Archsage in the Land of Challenge, available as downloadable content from Vol. 3 of the Expansion Pass. Clearing this challenge with at least a B rank for the first time will unlock the Throwback A outfit for Taion and clearing with at least A rank for the first will unlock the Throwback A outfit for Eunie.

Gauntlet: Pro is an Archsage's Gauntlet Challenge in . It can be challenged by talking to the Nopon Archsage in the Land of Challenge, available as downloadable content from Vol. 3 of the Expansion Pass. Clearing this challenge with at least B rank for the first time will unlock the Throwback A outfit for Mio, and clearing with at least A rank for the first will unlock the Throwback A outfit for Noah. After Stage 70, enemy attacks will deal irreducible extra damage and the Invincible buff will have no effect.
The Gaur Viaduct (Japanese: , Gauru Burijji) is a location in , located on the Aurora Shelf.

The Gelgemos Garrison (Japanese: , Gerugeimu Chūtonchi) is a location in , located at The Ragmos Desolation. It is the remains of the Old Gelgemos Gate from the Kingdom of Tantal. There is a Keves Outpost occupied by Keves Forces here.
Gem Unlock Kits are Key Items in . They can be used to unlock Gem slots for the party. There are twelve of them in total in the Cent-Omnia Region.
The Funbowl Recipe is a Key Item in . It allows the party to cook Fish-and-Fungi Funbowl at Rest Spots. It is obtained upon completing The Very Lost Nopon.
Georgie's Ask is a Standard Quest in . The Open-Air Dining Space is discovered after this quest is completed.

Future Awaits is the ending theme of . It was composed by Yasunori Mitsuda. Although Tetsuya Takahashi came up with the original lyrics, the English translation was provided by Lisa Gomamoto. Joanne Hogg lent her voice for the song. At Our Life's End is a piano arrangement of Future Awaits that plays on the title screen and during certain story events. Future Awaits is also featured as an available karaoke song in Karaoke JOYSOUND for Nintendo Switch. It also plays during Monolith Soft's 25th Anniversary Movie, and has been slightly remixed so that the backing guitar is more prominent.
Game Skewers are a Meal item in . They can be cooked at Rest Spots. It is unlocked by obtaining the Skewers Recipe.
Georgie's Special Curry is a Meal item in . It can be cooked at Rest Spots. It is unlocked by obtaining the Curry Recipe. It is Georgie's special family curry passed down to her by Giorgio.
Ftheri Torpedo Wrap is a Meal item in . It can be cooked at Rest Spots. It is unlocked by obtaining the Torpedo Wrap Recipe.

Georgie is an NPC in . She is the granddaughter of Giorgio from , and is likely the daughter of Paola. She can be found in the Central Plaza of Colony 9. Her Community is gained when talking to her after completing Georgie's Ask, acquiring all ten cooking recipes, and conversing with her twice. Like her grandfather, she can cook her family's special curry. She asks Shulk and the party to help build a canteen for the colony and to gather Dance Apples for her curry.
The Garrison Key is a Key Item in . It is a key that opens the Lumos Garrison gates, and it is found near the garrison outposts.
Galde Volffs are Normal Minor Enemies in . They are members of the Volff family, and can be found at level 16 in the Enemy Territory to the northeast of the Clifftop Camp on the Aurora Shelf.

Garfont Mercenaries is a Field Track from , composed by Kenji Hiramatsu. It is track nine of disc two from the Xenoblade 2 Original Soundtrack, and track nine of disc seven from the Xenoblade Original Soundtrack Trinity Box. This song plays during the day in Garfont Village.
Getting Qlued In is a Heart-to-Heart in . It is located by the Barista Court in the Commercial District of New Los Angeles between Neilnail and Cross anytime.
Ghost Acolytes are Main Bosses in . They are four members of the Ghost family that are fought at level 50 near the South Coast of Oblivia during Chapter 13 (Act 1).
The Ghost Crusader is a Main Boss in . It is a member of the Ghost family that is fought at level 54 on the Delusians North Summit in Sylvalum during Chapter 13 (Act 2).
Ghost A is a special Holofigure in . It can be obtained from Glossolalia, the Allochthon in Oblivia.
Ghost B is a special Holofigure in . It can be obtained from Apocalypsis, the Sacrificant in Sylvalum.

Ghost Cathedrals are normal Minor enemies in . They are members of the Ghost family. They can be found at level 54-55 floating near Dematerialization zones in Primordia, Noctilum, Oblivia, Sylvalum, and Cauldros during and after Chapter 13 (Act 2).

Ghost Martyrs are enemies in . They are members of the Ghost family. They can be found at level 99 after being summoned by Apocalypsis, the Sacrificant's art: Nascent Howl of Offering. They are not registered in the Enemy Index.

Full Metal Hairs I are light head armour in . They can be obtained by achieving a score of 2000 for the first time with Reyn in the Score Attack course Caterpile Circuit. They can also be purchased from Time Attack for 2,500 Noponstones. They can only be worn by Reyn.

Full Metal Hairs II are light head armour in . They can be obtained by winning with Reyn for the first time on the Battle Race course Twilight Speedway. They can also be purchased from Time Attack for 3,800 Noponstones. They can only be worn by Reyn.

Full Metal Tops I are light torso armour in . They can be obtained by achieving a score of 2200 for the first time with Reyn in the Score Attack course Jungle Rumble. They can also be purchased from Time Attack for 4200 Noponstones. They can only be worn by Reyn.

Full Metal Tops II are light torso armour in . They can be obtained by winning with Reyn for the first time on the Battle Race course Midnight Forest. They can also be purchased from Time Attack for 6300 Noponstones. They can only be worn by Reyn.

Untamed Shoes II are light feet armour in . They can be obtained by winning with Reyn for the first time on the Battle Race course Colony 9 Wild Ride. They can also be purchased from Time Attack for 4500 Noponstones. They can only be worn by Reyn.

Full Metal Greaves I are light feet armour in . They can be obtained by achieving a score of 2800 for the first time with Reyn in the Score Attack course Rural Road. They can also be purchased from Time Attack for 3000 Noponstones. They can only be worn by Reyn.

Full Metal Leggings II are light legs armour in . They can be obtained by winning with Reyn for the first time on the Battle Race course Blizzard Rally. They can also be purchased from Time Attack for 4900 Noponstones. They can only be worn by Reyn.

Full Metal Leggings I are light legs armour in . They can be obtained by achieving a score of 2600 for the first time with Reyn in the Score Attack course Valak Slalom. They can also be purchased from Time Attack for 3300 Noponstones. They can only be worn by Reyn.

Full Metal Arms II are light arms armour in . They can be obtained by winning with Reyn for the first time on the Battle Race course Alcamoth at Dawn. They can also be purchased from Time Attack for 2400 Noponstones. They can only be worn by Reyn.

Full Metal Arms I are light arms armour in . They can be obtained by achieving a score of 2400 for the first time with Reyn in the Score Attack course Alcamoth Orbital. They can also be purchased from Time Attack for 1600 Noponstones. They can only be worn by Reyn.

The Ge Jewhe's Dagger is an Important Item in . It is collected from the White Whale debris at the North Coast in Oblivia during the course of Until the End and choosing B route, meaning by speaking to Ge Jewhe at the Boxtrap Checkpoint before getting Vi Sezha's Bracelet or by choosing "Nod".
Gattle is an NPC in . He is an Urayan who can be found in Torika Alley in Fonsa Myma in the Kingdom of Uraya during the quest Farewell, Good Friend.
Gamoosah is an NPC in . She is an elderly Urayan who can be found just outside of Fonsa Myma's Entertainment District in the Kingdom of Uraya.

Germon is an NPC in . He is a Nopon who appears on the roofs of the Admar Storage Zone in the Empire of Mor Ardain during The Ties That Bind. He is part of a cult that attempts to perform a ritual called the Rite of Erasure in order to summon a Nopon demon called Lord Moe. However, a Gluttonous Pterix is summoned instead. He is unable to be spoken to.

Fuel Recovery Probes are types of Data Probes in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They boost fuel recovery for parked Skells. They are effective throughout the entire region in which the probe is installed. One is received for completing Chapter 10. Another is received for completing the Noctilum Collectopedia.

Glossy Grady Fans are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be dropped by Lunar Gradies in Eryth Sea, or traded for with Vidian and Zel Argentis. According to their description, they are brightly-shining fans that give the possessor a lust for money. Two are needed for Material Quest 1 from Alcamoth.

Gold Burdocks (Japanese: , Gōrudo Gobou) are collectables in . They can be found in the Eryth Sea. According to their description, cooking them longer creates extra sweetness and an eponymous golden colour. Three are required for the Timed Quest Collection Quest 1 at Alcamoth.

Giorgio (Japanese: , Kopamu) is a Homs in . He is a chef who can be found in his stall near the Ether Light in the south Commercial District of Colony 9. He has one daughter, Paola. The top of his stall is marked with a sign that has a spoon and fork crossing over a plate. In , Georgie is stated to be Giorgio's granddaughter. He is mentioned by Shulk during the Quest Georgie's Ask when Georgie serves Matthew some curry, and Shulk says that it is Giorgio's curry. Georgie later mentions how Shulk once got Giorgio some Dance Apples for his curry and saved Giorgio's reputation.

Gluttonous Eugen (Japanese: , Bōshoku no Oigen) is a Unique Monster in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is a member of the Brog family, and can be found in Vilia Lake in Tephra Cave at level 11. It drops Brog Smelling Salts, one lot of which is needed to complete Tephra Cave's Material Quest 2.

Gorman (Japanese: , Gēruman) is a Homs in Xenoblade Chronicles. He can be found in the Refugee Camp on Bionis' Leg between 21:00 and 06:00, and later moves back to Colony 6 along with the other residents of the Refugee Camp, and can be found there between 18:00 and 06:00. He is said to be Otharon's rival.

Gowago (Japanese: , Gowagowā) is a Nopon in . He can be found at 21:00 on the north side of Riki's House. If he has been recruited to Colony 6, he will be by the Junks at the Nopon houses during the day.

The Giants' Mirror is a Key Item in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is needed for The Giants' Treasure. It can be found on Bionis' Leg in the Daksha Shrine. The level 32 Unique Monster, the Clifftop Bayern, is guarding it, although it is not necessary to defeat it to obtain the item.

Giant Hornets (Japanese: , Oojirobachi) are collectables in . They can be found in Colony 9. According to their description, they are giant white hornets so heavy that they squash any flower they alight on. One is needed for Collection Quest 4 in Colony 9.

Gold Dust Illusions (Japanese: , Sakin no Maboroshi) are collectables in . They can be found on Bionis' Leg. According to their description, Shulk was starry-eyed when he named them and they are sands that shine a beautiful gold.

Gogols (Japanese: , Gogōru; English dub: , rhyming with ogle) are an ape-like family of enemies in the . They are very large and often high level. Gogols undergo a minor appearance change between games; in and they have manes instead of the hair spike they had in . They also gain slight more life-like anatomy.

Golden Cogs (Japanese: , Kin'iro Haguruma) are collectables in . They are part of the Other page of the Collectopaedia, and can only be acquired by trading with Oleksiy after he moves to Colony 6. According to their description, they are gearwheels fully made of gold an they could not work in any known machine. Obtaining one will unlock the "Shining Impracticality" achievement.

Gold Caterpillars (Japanese: , Koganeimomushi) are collectables in . They can be found in Tephra Cave. According to their description, they are insect larvae that sparkle in shiny gold for a few hours after hatching. Nine are required for the Timed Quest Looking for Gold Bugs.

Gold Condensers (Japanese: , Gōrudo Kondensa ) are collectables in . They can be found in Sword Valley and Colony 6 after the events at the Mechonis Core. According to their description, they are metallic and thus conductive, and people hesitate to use them.
Giant Attack! (Japanese: , Kyojin no Shūgeki) is a quest in . It can be received from Lalapa in the Chief's Residence in Frontier Village. If Riki is in the active party, he will comment.

Golden Beetroots (Japanese: , Gōruden Suika, Golden Watermelon) are collectables in . They can be found on the Fallen Arm. According to their description, they are a beetroot variety considered the best on the Mechonis and they are harvested frozen.

Gilder Cockroaches (Japanese: , Mekkitapira) are collectables in . They can be found in the Central Factory and in Colony 6 after the events at the Mechonis Core. They are apparently a recently discovered species, as little is known about them aside from their speed.

The Glowing Obelisk (Japanese: , Kōkyū no Oberisuku) is a landmark in . It is located in Satorl Marsh, just east of Exile Fortress. Shulk and his friends rest here when travelling up Bionis, saying the light from it should keep away monsters. The Obelisk is of ancient High Entia work and the light it emits is Ether.
Glass Rods (Japanese: , Gurasuroddo) are weapons in . They are staves wielded by Melia. It can be be acquired by trading with Talia who can be found in Eryth Sea.

Gracielle Helms (Japanese: , Gurashieru Herumu) are heavy head armour in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be dropped with no slots by Laeklit Mammuts, and can be obtained as a quest reward after completing Vidian Rescue Mission.
Gracielle Arms are heavy arms armour in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be obtained as a quest reward after completing Vidian Rescue Mission.
Gracielle Cuisses are heavy legs armour in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be dropped by various enemies.
Gracielle Greaves are heavy feet armour in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be obtained as a quest reward after completing Vidian Rescue Mission, and can be dropped by Bagrus Nebulae.
Giant Guarders (Japanese: , Gigantogādā) are weapons in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are gunlances wielded by Reyn. They can only be obtained through purchase from one shop in Colony 6.
Goliath (Japanese: , Jūken Goriasu, Heavy Sword Goliath) is a weapon in . It is a gunlance wielded by Reyn.

Gladiator Biters (Japanese: , Tōshi no Kamukamu) are weapons in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are biters that can be wielded by Riki. They can be acquired by purchasing them at the Frontier Village Weapon Shop and at Colony 6 Shop 4 for 8,700 G. It can also be acquired by trading with Lupa who can be found in Frontier Village or by trading with Neonik who can be found in Colony 6.
Grace Blades (Japanese: , Gureisuburēdo) are weapons in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are twin blades wielded by Fiora. They can only be acquired from one shop, in Colony 6.

Glory Gauntlets are medium arms armour in Xenoblade Chronicles. They have the highest Physical and Ether Defences of any medium arm armour. They are mostly dropped by Superbosses. They are one of three pieces of armour that possess a 45% Haste gem. Since Haste is normally a weapon gem, wearing these gauntlets effectively switches the use of the more limited weapon gem slot for an armour gem slot.

Grace Gloves are light arms armour in Xenoblade Chronicles. They have the best Physical and Ether Defence of any light arms armour in the game. They can be found in the Imperial Treasury in the High Entia Tomb, along with Grace Shoes, but are not otherwise available. The cloth used in their construction is said to be pure ether.

Grace Shoes are light feet armour in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be found in the Imperial Treasury in the High Entia Tomb, along with Grace Gloves. The cloth that makes up the shoes is derived from ether.

Glory Boots are medium feet armour in Xenoblade Chronicles. They have the highest Physical and Ether Defences of any medium foot armour. Like the other pieces in the Glory Set they can be dropped by the Superbosses.

Grace Caps (Japanese: , Gureisu Kyappu) are light head armour in Xenoblade Chronicles. They have the highest Physical Defence of any light head armour in the game, although Master Glasses have a higher Ether Defence. They are not dropped or carried by any enemies, and can only be obtained once per playthrough. After the party obtains the High Entia Emblem, a Grace Cap can be found behind a High Entia Door near the Sororal Statues in Satorl Marsh. To reach it, the party needs to ride the lift and jump off it near the top of its path, where a pale round disc can be seen.

Glory Gear (Japanese: , Gurōrī Gia) is medium head armour in Xenoblade Chronicles. It has the highest Physical and Ether Defences of any medium head armour. Like the other pieces in the Glory Set, it can be dropped by the Superbosses.
Grace Bottoms are light leg armour in Xenoblade Chronicles. They have the highest Physical and Ether Defence of any light leg armour in the game.

Glory Leggings are medium legs armour in Xenoblade Chronicles. They have the highest Physical and Ether Defences of any medium leg armour. Like the other pieces in the Glory Set they can be dropped by the Superbosses.

The Giant Mechon Debris (Japanese: , Kyodaina Kishinhei no Zangai) is a landmark in . It is located on the lower level of the Fallen Arm, at the southeast side of the Hidden Machina Village, at the base of Digit 1. It appears to be the remains of a Mechon Fortress Unit. There is an Ice Ether Gear deposit at its base. It is surrounded by various non-aggressive enemies; Lampo Ponios and Happiness Fliers during the day, and Caelum Volffs and Tramont Wisps during the night. A Lelepago Pterix periodically circles the area.

Gluttony Gogols are enemies in . They are members of the Gogol family, and can be found at level 78 north of Raguel Bridge and on the rocky platforms north of Raguel Lake on Bionis' Leg. They are always accompanied by two Greed Gogols. They can drop the Gogol Horns needed for A Token of Friendship and Colony 6 Reconstruction.

Glowmoss Lake (Japanese: , Hikari Goke no Chiteiko) is a Secret Area in . It is located on the ground floor of the Ether Mine. It is a lake found by following a long tunnel south from Test Pit 1. The Unique Monster Elegant Marin is found here, along with two Materia Krabbles and Rock Krabbles. On the other shore of Glowmoss Lake, there is a Water Ether Crystal deposit. During What is Courage?!, Ewan will appear here if the party chooses to visit the Ether Mine before Satorl Marsh. He will ask the party to defeat the Elegant Marin.

Glowing Wisp Fluid is a rare material in Xenoblade Chronicles. It can be dropped by Wisps on Kneecap Hill and the Bionis' Leg at night, or traded for. According to their description, they are liquids that emit an ethereal glow and they are used as simple lamps. Five are needed for Emergency Treatment.
Goldi Kromars are enemies in . They are members of the Kromar family, and can be found at level 86 in the Eryth Sea. They are Sight Category monsters.

The Giants are an extinct race in that once lived on Bionis. They were extant alongside the High Entia and Machina before the conflict between Bionis and Mechonis, having arisen on the Bionis' Shoulder and spread across the Bionis, but died out before the events of the main game. Their ruins exist all over the world, but details of their life and disappearance are shrouded in mystery.
Good Footing (Japanese: , Fukitobi Teikō, Blow-Down Resist) is a Gem in Xenoblade Chronicles that increases resistance to Blow-Down. Good Footing does not prevent knockback. __TOC__

This quest will expire after the events at the Mechonis Core. Going Out to Play (Japanese: , Musuko ga Soto de Asoberu Yōni) is a Timed Quest in Xenoblade Chronicles. It can be received from Popipo, just northeast of the Main Entrance of Alcamoth. She can be found next to the fountain from around 06:00 to 18:00. If Reyn is in the active party, he will comment.

Ghostly Mahatos (Japanese: , Kidō no Mahatosu) is a Unique Monster in . It is a Gigas-type member of the Telethia family, and can be found at level 76 near a doughnut-shaped platform west of the Terminal Nerve Tower.

Glacier Elements are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can only be dropped by Frost Nebulae in Satorl Marsh. Glacier Elements are not otherwise available. According to their description, they are ice elements that instantly creates an ice-sheet around the holder. One Glacier Element is needed for Replica Monado 3.

Glory Armour is medium torso armour in Xenoblade Chronicles. It has the highest Physical and Ether Defences of any medium torso armour. Like the other pieces in the Glory Set, it is only dropped by enemies that are around level 96 and above, including all of the Superbosses.
Gracielle Chests are heavy torso armour in Xenoblade Chronicles.

Graceful Holand (Japanese: , Yūgen no Hōrando) is a Unique Monster in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is a member of the Nebula family, and can be found at level 19 on the Splintered Path in Colony 6, northeast of the Drainage Outlet during rain.

Glacier Acon (Japanese: , Hyōga no Eikōn) is a Unique Monster in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is a Mechon, and can be found at level 52 in the 1st Turbine Room of Galahad Fortress, although later can be found in the Main Control Room.

Glorious Jurom (Japanese: , Ranman no Shuromu, Arrogant Shuromu) is a Unique Monster in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is a Mechon, and can be found at level 55 at the Ether Blast Furnace in Galahad Fortress.

Gigas Telethia (Japanese: , Gigāsu Tereshia) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are Gigas-type members of the Telethia family, and can be found at level 75 in Bionis' Interior. One of them can be found on a platform along the central path through the Venous Plexus.

Glowing Upa Seeds are rare materials in . They can be dropped by various Upas in Satorl Marsh and can be traded for in Satorl Marsh when Ewan is there. According to their description, they are seeds that glow in water and they also look great in cocktails. Four of them are needed for Making Camp.

The Giants' Key is a Key Item in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is required for The Giants' Key. It can be found in Satorl Marsh on a high plateau southeast of the Silent Obelisk. The Giants' Key can be found by traveling southeast from the Silent Obelisk until three paths appear, then taking the left path which eventually leads to a tunnel. On the other side of the tunnel is a plateau. When The Giants' Key is active, the plateau will be guarded by Deluded Igna. Once they have been defeated, the Giants' Key can be found buried near a tree on the plateau.

The Glowmoss Trihenge (Japanese: , Hikarigoke no Sansekichū) is a landmark in . It is located in Makna Forest, east of the Windmill Pavilion and north of Precipice Bridge. There are no enemies near it.
Gogol Snack Stashes are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be obtained from the Dogmatic Gogol in Satorl Marsh. Gogol Snack Stashes are also available via trade.

Giant Sauros Fangs are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be dropped by Deinos Sauros and Magnificent Digalus in Makna Forest, or traded for with En Argentis during Stopping the Elopement in Tephra Cave. According to their description, they are fangs from the king of monsters which can bite through anything.

Ghost Masks are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be traded for with Jer'ell when she is in Alcamoth. They are held by the Wizard Entia for one battle but are not obtainable from drops nor by using Yoink!. According to their description, they are masks of an ether expert and they say 'Aim for high office' on the back.
Giant Queen Jaws are rare materials in . They can only be obtained through trading.

Giant King Jaws are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. It can be obtained from the Clifftop Bayern at Daksha Shrine on Bionis' Leg. Giant King Jaws are also available via trading with Dulland. According to their description, they look enormous up close and they weigh between 100g and 40kg.

Glowing in the Night (Japanese: , Mayonaka no Fushigina Hikari, Midnight's Marvelous Light) is a Heart-to-Heart in . It is located at the Spring of Grief in Tephra Cave, between Riki and Dunban at purple affinity. It can only be viewed at night.

Giant Grexes (Japanese: , Masshibu Rupusu, Massive Lupus) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Grex family, and can be found at level 22-25 near North Janpath Plain, and level 21-23 or 27 at Grieving Plains in Primordia. Three must be defeated using specific weapons to complete Proficiency Exam 7, which in turn must be completed before owning a Skell.

Glennar (Japanese: , Gurennā; English dub: or ) is a Main Boss in Xenoblade Chronicles X. He is fought at level 10 in Seaswept Base in Primordia during Chapter 3, accompanied by two Prone Ruffians. He is commanding the Seaswept Base's Prone squad. His Beam Gatling attack can rack up damage quickly when combined with the Debilitating Beam used by one of the Prone Ruffians.

Goliath, the Stronghold (Japanese: , Jōsai Goraiasu) is a Tyrant in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a member of the Vigent family. It can be found at level 50 at North Cinderdunes in Sylvalum. Defeating it is required to complete the eponymous Basic Mission Goliath, the Stronghold.

Gigio (Japanese: , Jījo) is an NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. He is first found in Noctilum, west of Potter's Rock. After completing Data Miner, he can be found on Division Drive in the Administrative District of New Los Angeles. He is a member of the Outfitters Division, and is implied to be working specifically for Sakuraba Industries.

Goblin's Narrow (Japanese: , Kooni Sebaji) is an area in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located southwest of Tripod Rock in Noctilum and continues southwest to Sunlit Spring. It is where the party meets L for the first time. The FN Site 219 is located here.

Glowing Ciniculas (Japanese: , Gurou Vasaruto) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Cinicula family, and can be found at level 44-46 at the Anvil Sandplain in Sylvalum. The level 46 Glowing Ciniculas are much larger than the lower-leveled ones and burrow out of the ground upon spawning.
Ghostwalker is a Support Battle Art in . It grants the user the Decoy buff, while also granting total evasion for the art animation.

Glaive Insidias (Japanese: , Gureibu Parako) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Insidia family, and can be found at level 41-44 near Victory Rock and Lake Basel in Oblivia.

Gloam Turbas (Japanese: , Guromu Kurekusu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Turba family, and can be found at level 34-35 at the Secluded Lava Lake in Sylvalum, which can be found in a cave right next to the FN Site 401. Six must be defeated for Turba Tracker.
Giogion is a Ma-non in Xenoblade Chronicles X. He can be found at the Armory Alley in the Administrative District of New Los Angeles.

Goliath Sylooth (Japanese: , Goraiasu Shirūsu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Sylooth family, and one can be found at level 50 at Rustpool Banks, in front of the Lakeview Stronghold southern exit in Noctilum.
Giotto is a NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. He can be found at BLADE Concourse in the Administrative District of New Los Angeles. He is a member of the Interceptors Division.
Giddy Adseculas (Japanese: , Shirī Apisu, Silly Apis) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Adsecula family, and can be found at level 44 at Coil Tree Cape in Noctilum.
Golden Sardines (Japanese: , Iwasshyi) are unique collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Primordia.

Go-rha, the Guardian Deity (Japanese: , Shugoshin Go-raa) is a Tyrant in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a Xe-dom mech and can be found dormant at level 60 in the lake below Yagami's Vista in Noctilum. Go-rha reflects all attributes, so it is necessary to create and equip augments that negate attribute reflects.
Glowing Liceors (Japanese: , Gurōin Kurāra) are minor enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Liceor family, and can be found at level 25-30 near East Ciel Sandsea in Sylvalum.
Gina is a NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. She can be found near Barista Court in the Commercial District of New Los Angeles.
Gormless Monkeys (Japanese: , Monkifurato) are rare collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Oblivia.

Godmelons (Japanese: , Goddomeron) are prime collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Noctilum, in particular near the river below Divine Roost, around FN Site 202 or at Elephant's Trunk.

Gluttonutan Clays (Japanese: , Ūtan Nendo) are common collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Noctilum, in particular at FN Sites 220 or 221. Ten pieces are needed for Material Hunt A.
Gluttonutans (Japanese: , Moraūtan) are rare collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Noctilum.
Goddess's Kisses (Japanese: , Megami no Kuchidzuke) are prime collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Primordia, in particular the north coast near Arendt Bridge.
Gleaming Magnets (Japanese: , Kōki no Magunetto) are rare collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Noctilum.

Glassy Crickets (Japanese: , Garasu Suzumushi) are rare collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Sylvalum, in particular in North Hardheart Canyon or Sylvalum Searoad. On the FrontierNav, it is located on the upper-left of FN Site 420 (farthest Miranium deposit to the right). Three of them are needed for A Crickety Cure.
Gold Papils (Japanese: , Gōrudo Papirio) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Papil family, and can be found at level 44-46 at Floating Reef and Demon's Pocket in Oblivia.
Gibney Jackals (Japanese: , Gibunijakkā) are prime collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Cauldros.

Gradivus, the Headless Emperor (Japanese: , Kubinashi Kōtei Guradeusu) is a Tyrant in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a member of the Millesaur family. It can be found at level 71 at the North Coast in Oblivia after completing Chapter 12. It can summon Parasite Gerrids for assistance. When it does so, it changes the attribute of the projectile arts it uses. While Gradivus may not be as offensively capable as higher-leveled Tyrants, it does have the largest amount of HP of any enemy.

Giraffin, the Old Hand (Japanese: , Rōren no Jīrafu) is a Tyrant in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a member of the Lepyx family, and can be found at level 41 at the South Silent Sandsea in Sylvalum, immediately north of FN Site 413. It can drop the Holofigure Lepyx B.

Gotthard, the Intimidating (Japanese: , Kyōkaku no Gottoharuto) is a Tyrant in . It is a member of the Auravis family. It can be found at level 61 in the sky above the northmost part of the Yawning Giant in Oblivia.

Gi-zho, the Iron Deity (Japanese: , Tetsukishin Gi-zou) is a Tyrant in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a Xe-dom machine. It can be found at level 79 south of Kw'arah Villa inside the southeast-most mining frigate in Cauldros.

Golden Mortifole Feathers are common materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from golden Mortifoles. Two of them are needed to complete the related Basic Mission Indigen Investigation.

Giant Sacrifoles (Japanese: , Masshibu Kurusuta) are minor enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Sacrifole family, and can be found at level 41-50 in Sylvalum at Lake Ciel. They either float above the surface of the water or are hidden amongst patches of smaller flowers.

Golden Yggralith Hearts are intergalactic materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are dropped by Yggralith Zero if the fighting team drops its RP to zero. They can also be obtained by exchanging Reward Tickets at the Network Console. Two of them are needed to create an Ares 90 Skell. One apiece are needed to craft the True Comm, True Cords, True Bangle L, True Bangle R, and True Plastron armor set.

Gi Zang (Japanese: , Gi Zangu) is a NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. He is a Wrothian, and can be found in at the Ruins on the Sandbank in Oblivia, west of the BLADE Tower or southwest of the Mimeosome Maintenance Center in the Administrative District, at the Titan's Table in Cauldros, or in the Port Side of the Ma-non Ship.

Gi Ziorde (Japanese: , Gi Zorude) is a NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. He can be found at Anvil Rock Two in Sylvalum then at the Outfitters Test Hangar in the Industrial District of New Los Angeles during the Normal Mission Two Warriors.

Gi Ziordo (Japanese: , Gi Zorudo) is a NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. He can be found at King's Falls in Oblivia then at the Outfitters Test Hangar in the Industrial District of New Los Angeles during the Normal Mission Two Warriors.
Golden Progen Wings are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from blue Progen.

Gold Courage (Japanese: , Gōrudo Bureibu) is a Mission Exclusive Secondary Boss in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a Human-Made Skell piloted by Roselle and is fought at level 32 in Primordia during A Dubious Operation.

Golden Puffs are common materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from the tail appendages of yellow Mephites in Sylvalum or Cauldros. Six of them are needed during My Angel, My Lana. They are also needed to engineer AppendLost.ATK-UP augments.

Gorkwa Games (Japanese: , Riborutanto Chūdoku, Revoltant Addiction) is a Normal Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It can be received from Troylan in the Ma-non Ship. Troylan gives their broken gorkwa and asks the party to have Lulladu fix it.

Good Neighbors (Japanese: , Kyōsei to Kyōzon, Symbiosis and Coexistence) is a Normal Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It can be received from Tan'celeg in the Outfitters Test Hangar in the Industrial District. Although it's not required the Basic Mission Tech Supply can be used to locate this mission.

Giant Jade Pearls are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be dropped by the Liceors in Sylvalum or purchased for 66 Reward Tickets at the Network Console in the BLADE Barracks. They are components for Rank X - XX EXP Boost augments.

Going Home is a Heart-to-Heart in . It is located in the BLADE Barracks in New Los Angeles, between Elma and Cross at night-time. The dialogue varies depending on whether Chapter 12 has been completed.
Gold Monoceros Horns are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from blue Monoceroses in Cauldros.

The Gleaming Sphinxes (Japanese: , Ryuosu Gurinto) are Mission Exclusive Enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are level 80 members of the Sphinx family. Two of them must be defeated at Oblivia's Keegan Ridge during Then and Now. Their arts include Bone Charge (physical), Double Claw (electrical), Explosion (fire), Fire Breath (fire), Flame Mortar (fire), Flash (ether), Roar (physical), Sharpen Claw, Sky Savage (electrical), Slash (physical), and Tail Swing (physical).

Going Viral (Japanese: , Ijō Zōka, Abnormal Increase) is a Normal Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It can be received from Julius on the Commercial District's West Melville Street in New Los Angeles. Although it is not required the Basic Mission Anomaly Analysis can be used to locate this mission.
Gold Nopopotamus Card is an Important Item in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is obtained from Ton'barac and is needed to complete Trade Agreement.

The Girhi Caladar (Japanese: , Giri Kakara) is a Mission Exclusive Secondary Boss in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is the Caladar Skell piloted by Da Girhi fought at level 41 at Stickstone Rise in Primordia during The Queen Is Dead.
Giant Blue Pearls are common materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from blue Liceors. Two of them are needed for The Jewelmonger.
Go Belg (Japanese: , Go Berugu) is an NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. He is a Wrothian, and can be found at the Wrothian Stronghold in Oblivia at night.

Girls' Night Out is Hope's second Heart-to-Heart in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It occurs between Hope and Cross in the evening, by the red bench northeast of East Melville Street, in the Commercial District of New Los Angeles.

Good Fortun (Japanese: , Forutun Sōdatsu, The Struggle for Fortun) is a Normal Mission in . It becomes available after both Chapter 10 and Alex's Last Stand have been completed, and can be received from HT665: Erio in the west corner of the Central Industrial District. The Basic Mission The Call to Counterattack can be used to locate this mission, but is not a prerequisite. Completing it earns the "Mechanical Immigration" achievement.

Gold Rush (Japanese: , Utsusemi, The Mortal Coil) is a Normal Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It becomes available after completing The Celeste Three and triggering a cutscene by encountering Ga Bewhe near BLADE Barracks. It can be received from Adolphus in the Industrial District of New Los Angeles, under the crane platform southeast of Professor B's Lab at late night. Law and Orders will also be triggered while pursuing the first objective. After this mission is completed, Ga Bewhe will appear on a plateau northwest of FN Site 312 when it is raining. If spoken to, she will express regrets about taking the white gold and give 200,000 Credits.
Giant Cavities are unique materials in . They can be obtained from Balaenas.

Gold Ceto Membranes are unique materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from yellow Cetos in Noctilum and Oblivia. They are components in X, XV, and XX Ether Res Up and SpecUp.ETHER-RES augments.

Go Sirho (Japanese: , Go Shiro) is an NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. She is a Wrothian, and can be found in the east part of the Commercial District, then at the Pathfinders' section of Division Drive in the Administrative District of New Los Angeles at night. She is found on Oblivia's South Coast during Wrothian Innovation, practicing installing data probes on FN Site 317.
Go Rogan (Japanese: , Go Rogan) is an NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. He is a Wrothian, and intially can be found on the Deck of the Ma-non Ship. After The Lurker he moves to the Port Side.
The Gorkwa is an Important Item in Xenoblade Chronicles X. Orleron asks the party to find it during Child of Mira.
Gnarlbranch Sap is an Important Item in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It can be found in Noctilum's Divine Roost, and is needed during Herbivores, Unite!.
Giving It Away is Hope's third Heart-to-Heart in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It occurs in the morning in the Central Industrial District of New Los Angeles.
Glamor Girl is a Basic Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a request from a Female BLADE and the primary destination is Sylvalum.
Giant Cinicula Jaws are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from Ciniculas.

Goetia's Black Heels are prime materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from Goetia, or for 162 Reward Tickets at the Network Console in the BLADE Barracks. They are also given out as rewards for the Time Attack Mission Xeno from the Abyss. They are components in crafting the Masterstroke and Original weapons.

Gold Sylooth Braces are unique materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from Pyotr, the Shepherd, or for 114 Reward Tickets at the Network Console in the BLADE Barracks. They are components in creating X, XV, and XX Gravity Attack Plus and AttributeDmg.GRAV augments.

Golden Armor are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from the Vita, or for 66 Reward Tickets at the Network Console in the BLADE Barracks. They can also be earned for completing the Time Attack Mission Dark Matter Phantom.

Golden Blatta Wings are common materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from gold Blattas, or for 36 Reward Tickets at the Network Console in the BLADE Barracks. They are components in X, XV, and XX Physical Res Up and SpecUp.PHYS-RES augments.

Golden Cantor Teeth are unique materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from yellow/blue Cantors, for 108 Reward Tickets at the Network Console in the BLADE Barracks, or for 65 Material Tickets from the Material Market in .

Golden Gyrocompasses are common materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from silver Quos, or for 54 Reward Tickets at the Network Console in the BLADE Barracks. They are components for SpecUp.FUEL-BIND augments.

Golden Jewels are common materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from Saltats with gold balls, or for 42 Reward Tickets at the Network Console in the BLADE Barracks. They are components for all ranks of EXP Boost augments.

Golden Petramand Silk are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from Petramands with yellow acid sacs, or for 90 Reward Tickets at the Network Console in the BLADE Barracks. They are components for X, XV, and XX Crush: Gain TP and Crush.GP augments.

Golden Simius Manes are common materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from yellow-haired Simiuses, or for 54 Reward Tickets at the Network Console in the BLADE Barracks. They are components in I and V Cooldown Reducer and Custom.WP-SPEED augments.
Golden Stabilizers are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from the stabilizers of golden Fal-swos that have blue lights. One is needed to craft a Delta Bliss Multigun.
Golden Yggralith Nuts are unique materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from Yggralith Zero. They are components in the Regal series of BLADE Wear.

Golden Cedar are intergalactic materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are exclusively obtained from the gold Blattas in Sylvalum, and cannot be purchased elsewhere. They have no purpose except to be sold for a large amount of Credits.

Golden Chalices are intergalactic materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are exclusively obtained from the gold Blattas in Cauldros, and cannot be purchased elsewhere. They have no purpose except to be sold for a large amount of Credits.

Golden Fir Trees are intergalactic materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are exclusively obtained from the gold Blattas in Oblivia, and cannot be purchased elsewhere. They have no purpose except to be sold for a large amount of Credits.

Gold Ingots are intergalactic materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are exclusively obtained from the gold Blattas in Noctilum, and cannot be purchased elsewhere. They have no purpose except to be sold for a large amount of Credits.

Golden Medals are intergalactic materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are exclusively obtained from the gold Blattas in Primordia, Roimi, the Affluent and Agito, the Golden, and cannot be purchased elsewhere. They have no purpose except to be sold for a large amount of Credits.
Glossy Saltat Fans are common materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from Saltats.
Giant Falsaxum Jaws are rare materials in . They can be obtained from Falsaxum.
Gradivus is a Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It depicts Gradivus, the Headless Emperor as a millesaur variant. It can be obtained from it in Oblivia anytime after Chapter 12.

Gladiis Series is a Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It depicts Meredith & Co. Dual Swords. It is obtained as a reward for completing the Normal Mission Prone Sweet Prone. The Gladiis weapons available in-game are: * Archetype Gladiis * Iron Gladiis * Carbide Gladiis * Cermet Gladiis * Chrome Gladiis * Chromoly Gladiis * Cobalt Gladiis * Titanium Gladiis * Ceramic Gladiis * Diamond Gladiis

The Gigas Nopopotamus (Japanese: , Gigasu Nopohippo) are three Mission Exclusive Enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Potamuses commanded by Lularita and are fought at level 40 in the Outfitters Test Hangar in the Industrial District during the second battle of The Gauntlet.

Giant Bird Surge is a Squad Mission in . It is part of BLADE Mission No.14, and is unlocked when the Squad has completed the Squad Task of hunting four Ro-darm, the Demon Claws. It can be accepted at the Network Console in the BLADE Barracks.

Give No Ground is a Squad Mission in . It is part of BLADE Mission No.14, and is unlocked when the Squad has completed the Squad Task of hunting twenty Insectoids. It can be accepted at the Network Console in the BLADE Barracks.

Giant Skell Discovery is a Squad Mission in . It is part of BLADE Mission No.20, and is unlocked if the Skell Wreckage was examined during Unwelcome Guests. It can be accepted at the Network Console in the BLADE Barracks.
Gi Nogan (Japanese: , Gi Nogan) is an NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. He is a Wrothian, and can be found at the Wrothian Stronghold in Oblivia during the day.

Gi Bordo (Japanese: , Gi Borudo) is a Mission Exclusive Enemy in Xenoblade Chronicles X. He is a level 38-39 Wrothian and is fought alongside Da Dorde, Gu Galda, Zo Zongra in Sylvalum during the squad mission The Wrothian Four.
Gi Nagri (Japanese: , Gi Nagiri) is an NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. He is a Wrothian, and can be found at the Port Side of the Ma-non Ship in New Los Angeles.

Gone Berserk is a Time Attack Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is unlocked after Definian Downfall is completed, and features a level 55 version of the Rexoskell boss. It can be accepted at the Network Console in the BLADE Barracks.

Giant Proteins are common materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be obtained solely from Chimai Selua in the Bionis' Interior. Giant Proteins are not otherwise available. According to their description, they are proteins that are as big as an orange and are too big to be classed as molecules.
Gooey Gunge is a common material in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is dropped by various enemies on the Fallen Arm, and can also be traded for.
Golbogga's Disk is an Important Item in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It must be obtained from Toluera during the Normal Mission The Old Gods.

Gormott (Japanese: , Gūra, Gula; English dub: ) is a Titan in and . It is a large giraffe-like entity covered in lush green woodlands and plains. This titan was once an independent republic of the Gormotti people, but since conquest 50 years before the main story by the Empire of Mor Ardain, it is now known as the Gormott Province. While exploring Gormott, its head and his dorsal fin can be viewed moving. Nature is abundant on Gormott, covered in lush plains and forests, and the accessible areas are affected by the movements of the Cloud Sea. Gormott is still very fertile, which is why Mor Ardain desired it to become the new permanent home of the Ardainian people after their titan Mor Ardain

The Gormott Province (Japanese: , Gūra Ryō, lit. Gula Territory) is a Nation in . The region was once an independent nation from the Gormott Titan, but it fell under Ardainian control less than 50 years before Pyra's reawakening. This territory is home to the Gormotti people, whose main settlement is the town of Torigoth. Nature is abundant on Gormott, covered in lush plains and forests, and the accessible areas are affected by the movements of the Cloud Sea. This nation was initially called the Imperial Province of Gormott in early builds. __TOC__

The Goldmouth Return Port (Japanese: , Gorutomunto Kikan no Minato) is a landmark in . It is located in Goldmouth at the Argentum Trade Guild, and is the first landmark visited in the game. It leads into the Central Exchange. There are no enemies here except during Cargo Escort.

The Goldmouth Exit Dock (Japanese: , Gorutomunto Kadode no Minato) is a Location in . It is located in Goldmouth in the Argentum Trade Guild. After the events of Chapter 1, the Maelstrom is docked here.

Gottarm Drivers (Japanese: , Gōtama Doraibā) are enemies in . They are Drivers fought alongside their Blades. One can found at level 20 at the Stone Gate Ruins in the Kingdom of Uraya, alongside a Menes Driver and Martial Kamron.

Glamorous Alfred (Japanese: , Kowaku no Maririn) is a Unique Monster in . He is a member of the Arachno family and can be found at level 50 in the Chamber of Offering on the Mid Level of the Spirit Crucible Elpys. It can be reached by skip traveling to Stele of Judgment, turning around, and going through the tunnel to the Chamber of Offering. Alfred needs to be defeated to unlock Agate's level 5 Rhodochrosite Might, Zenobia's level 4 "The Indomitable" and Godfrey's level 5 Tough Break affinity rewards.

The Goldmouth Warehouse (Japanese: , Gorutomunto Sōko) is a landmark in . It is located near the Salvage Deck in the Argentum Trade Guild. The warehouse is owned by a Nopon named Rentarenta, who can be found standing near the front door. The warehouse has two entrances, both of which are initially locked: * The front door is in the northeast corner of the Salvage Deck. It can be unlocked by speaking to Rentarenta and paying to rent the warehouse. He first asks for 100,000 G, but if the party refuses to pay the full price he drops the price to 99,990 G (a discount of 10 G). * The back door is reached by jumping into the Cloud Sea and swimming around to a secret corridor on the north side of A
The Goldmouth Wheelhouse (Japanese: , Gorutomunto Sōdashitsu) is a Landmark in . It is located in Goldmouth of the Argentum Trade Guild. It is where Argentum's navigation controls are located.
The Goldmouth Res. Dist. (Japanese: , Gorutomunto Kyojūku) is a Location in . It is a residential area located in Goldmouth at the Argentum Trade Guild.
The Goldmouth Viewpoint (Japanese: , Gorutomunto Tenbō Dekki) is a location in . It is located in Goldmouth at the Argentum Trade Guild. There are no enemies here.
Goetuis Wharf #1 (Japanese: , Gōtoisuuto-kō Dai-ichi Sanbashi) is a Landmark in . It is located at Goetuis Port in the Indoline Praetorium.
Goetuis Wharf #2 (Japanese: , Gōtoisuuto-kō Dai-ni Sanbashi) is a Landmark in . It is located at Goetuis Port in the Indoline Praetorium.
Goetuis Port (Japanese: , Gōtoisuuto-kō) is a Location in . It is located in the Goetuis Port area of the Indoline Praetorium.

The Gotrock Oracle Ruins (Japanese: , Getorikusu Shintaku Atochi) is a location in . It is located on the Lower Level of the Cliffs of Morytha, beyond Jubilee Gate. It is the final location visited before the party descends to the Land of Morytha. Kasandra's Heart-to-heart, "Forward-Looking Woman", can be viewed here.

Gladiator Orion (Japanese: , Ōkaittōryū no Dan) is one of the Superbosses in . He is a Unique Monster and a Urayan Driver. He can be found at level 100 at the Hallowed Godswood Shrine on the Cliffs of Morytha. He is also fought during the Challenge Battle, Fiercest Faction.
Gormotti Fish Flakes are Seafood Pouch items in . They can be purchased from Tomi Fishmongers in Torigoth in the Gormott Province.
Gormotti Honeyteas are Drink Pouch items in . They can be purchased from Café Savvy run by Adwen in Torigoth in the Gormott Province.
Gormott Heads are Treasure items in . They can be purchased in Torigoth of the Gormott Province at Margia's Odds & Ends run by Kassa, or by Salvaging at any Gormott Salvage Point.
